attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: 'At the very least nobody has succeeded' is the minimum he commits to. Normalising to that weaker clause is faithful, and the scope is LLMs.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: efficiency means fewer compute resources for comparable work, and price cuts are excluded. The Nov 2022 to publication window comes from the surrounding text.

evidence.note: June 2023 documented deployment: the same Chatbot Arena traffic and models were served with 50% fewer GPUs after switching to vLLM. The developers report this about their own work, but the contract accepts a documented deployment, and it predates the post.

reviews.rationale: The contradiction condition only needs one documented implementation doing comparable LLM work with fewer computing resources during the period. The vLLM/LMSYS deployment (June 2023) served the same models and traffic with half the GPUs. That is a resource saving, not a price change. It is the developers' own account, but it is a dated, documented deployment of the kind the contract requires.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps his setting-aside of accuracy and speed 'performance' measures. It is a firm present-tense observation.

contract.note: Reading 'plateaued' as no materially new useful task capabilities, with accuracy and speed gains excluded, matches his 'does more' framing. The September 1–16 window and the line between a new capability and better accuracy are the evaluator's choices.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own o1 announcement (Sept 12, 2024). It mostly reports benchmark accuracy on existing task types, which the claim excludes, and it is a company disclosure.
Independent ARC Prize review (Sept 13, 2024). It reports better adaptation to novelty but scores near Claude 3.5 Sonnet, so it does not show materially new useful tasks.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows o1 improving on reasoning benchmarks, which mostly measure accuracy on existing task types that the claim sets aside. No contemporaneous evaluation shows materially new useful tasks, and none broadly confirms a plateau. Neither the support nor the contradiction condition is met.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion, drawing on press reporting he cites in the post.

semantics.note: Covers all three parts: both companies deeply unprofitable, pricing designed to win customers, and Anthropic on course to lose $2.7B in 2024. 'On course' is correctly read as the outlook at publication.

contract.note: Treating the figures as press estimates and 'on course' as an outlook is fair. Requiring separate evidence of pricing intent is reasonable, since losses alone don't show intent.

evidence.note: July 2024 press estimate from internal data: OpenAI could lose up to $5B in 2024. Anthropic's $2.7B is described as spending against small revenue, which still implies large losses.
Sept 24, 2024 report that Anthropic expects to lose over $2.7B this year, and that both companies are deep in the red. Published eight days after the post but well before the evaluation date.

reviews.rationale: Press estimates support the loss parts: large OpenAI losses and an Anthropic outlook of about $2.7B in losses, though the accounting basis varies between reports. Nothing in the packet addresses the claim that pricing was designed for customer acquisition rather than profit. The support condition needs all three parts, and nothing contradicts any of them, so the claim stays unresolved.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Firm conditional ('would'). Keeps the antecedent 'any of these lawsuits prevail', the stronger impact on Google and Meta, the retraining chain, the billions in cost and the efficacy loss.

contract.note: Requiring a merits victory on training liability, not procedural rulings or settlements, follows the context. Which cases count as 'these lawsuits' is not fully specified.

evidence.note: Feb 2026 discovery order in Andersen. Procedural only: no liability finding and no retraining remedy.
Tracker status as of Oct 2026: Andersen still in discovery with merits pending, so the antecedent has not occurred.
July 2026 approval of the Bartz settlement. The court rejected requests to delete models. This is a settlement over pirated books, not a qualifying training-liability victory.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent, a qualifying plaintiff merits victory on training liability, has not happened according to the evidence: Andersen remains in discovery and Bartz ended in a settlement. A conditional whose antecedent has not occurred is not scored, and no deadline was stated.
